inline_text:
### Project Name Neo4j Agent Memory ### Project Description Neo4j Agent Memory is an open-source, graph-native memory layer for AI agents. It gives agents three kinds of persistent memory in a single property graph: - Short-term memory: conversation history, stored as messages. - Long-term memory: a knowledge graph of entities and relationships. It uses the POLE+O model (Person, Object, Location, Event, Organization) and can be constrained by a user-defined ontology. - Reasoning memory: decision traces and tool calls, recorded as first-class nodes with provenance. The third layer is the differentiator. Most agent memory today stores conversations and retrieves them by vector similarity. That gives recall, but not understanding: the agent cannot ask what it decided last time, why, which tools it used, or whether it worked. Recording reasoning as structured graph data makes memory auditable and lets agents learn from their own past behavior. Graph structure supplies the relationships and multi-hop context. Vectors supply similarity. The project ships: - A typed Python SDK (neo4j-agent-memory on PyPI, Python 3.10–3.13) and a TypeScript SDK (@neo4j-labs/agent-memory on npm). - A Vercel AI SDK provider. - An MCP server with 16 tools on the self-hosted backend. - A multi-stage entity extraction pipeline (spaCy, GLiNER, LLM) with entity resolution and deduplication. - Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, and AWS Strands. - A conformance test suite that checks behavior across languages. LLM and embedding providers are pluggable: native adapters for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and sentence-transformers, with LiteLLM as a fallback for 100+ more. A fully local mode needs no LLM. Origin and history: Neo4j Labs started the project in January 2026, and the first release went to PyPI on January 22, 2026. There have been 15 Python releases through v0.6.0 (September 14, 2026), plus parallel TypeScript SDK releases. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and currently developed as a Neo4j Labs project, which means it is experimental and community-supported. Note on project naming: if the project is accepted the project would likely need to be renamed to remove the Neo4j trademark and indicate support for multiple backends (Context Graph Memory) or (Open Agent Memory). ### Alignment with AAIF Mission Alignment with AAIF Mission AAIF stewards open, interoperable infrastructure for agents that work across platforms. Its current projects cover several layers of that stack: - MCP connects agents to tools and data. - A2A connects agents to each other. - AGENTS.md carries instructions to agents. - goose provides an agent runtime. - agentgateway handles routing and policy. None of them covers persistent memory and state. Today every framework implements memory in its own incompatible way, so an agent's accumulated knowledge cannot move between frameworks, runtimes, or vendors. Neo4j Agent Memory addresses this with four pieces, all framework-neutral and model-neutral: - An open memory data model: three memory types plus the POLE+O schema. - A standard MCP tool surface for reading and writing memory. - Adapters for eight agent frameworks. - A conformance suite so independent implementations can show they behave the same. Neutral governance matters especially for memory. Memory holds an organization's most sensitive accumulated context, and enterprises will not commit that to a format controlled by one vendor. Under AAIF, we intend to separate the open specification and reference SDKs from any single storage backend. ### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects - MCP: The project ships an MCP server (Python via FastMCP, TypeScript via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk), so any MCP client can use memory without a framework-specific integration. We would contribute the memory tool profile back as a candidate pattern for MCP-based memory. - AGENTS.md: The repository maintains its own AGENTS.md. An included example shows coding agents sharing team memory, which complements AGENTS.md: AGENTS.md carries static instructions, and memory carries what agents learn over time. - goose: goose can attach the memory MCP server as an extension today. We'd like to work with goose maintainers on a first-class memory integration [not yet built]. - A2A: Reasoning memory records which agent made which decision, using which tools. That is the provenance layer multi-agent delegation needs. Shared memory across agents is a planned area of collaboration. - agentgateway: The MCP server can be deployed behind agentgateway for policy and observability. No dedicated integration exists yet. ### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption Use cases. - Personalized assistants that remember user preferences across sessions. - Commerce agents that ground recommendations in a product catalog plus customer context. In a reference implementation, bridging memory to the catalog graph cut a recommended project basket from $3,220 to $1,261 by using what the agent already knew about the customer. - Financial services advisors with an audit trail of agent decisions. - Retail and customer support assistants. - Shared team memory for coding agents. - Distilling reusable skills from an agent's recorded reasoning. Adoption signals (as of October 2026). - About 23,300 PyPI downloads in the last 30 days. - About 1,600 monthly npm downloads for the TypeScript SDK, plus about 290 for the Vercel AI SDK provider. - 575 GitHub stars. - Contributions from Persistent Systems in addition to Neo4j. - Integrations maintained for frameworks from Google, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, and others. - The project was presented at AI Engineer World's Fair ("Actionable Knowledge for Agents with Context Graphs"). ### Technical Committee Sponsor (if identified) _No response_ ### GitHub Repository URL https://github.com/neo4j-labs/agent-memory ### License Apache-2.0 ### Governance Model The project is currently maintained as a Neo4j Labs project. Maintainers employed by Neo4j review and merge pull requests and cut releases. Outside contributions are accepted through the public pull request process described in CONTRIBUTING.md. If accepted, the project will adopt the LF Minimum Viable Governance (MVG) framework. That includes a GOVERNANCE.md and a MAINTAINERS.md, a public process for nominating maintainers based on sustained contribution, and a stated goal of adding maintainers from outside Neo4j within 12 months. ### CI/CD & Release Workflow CI runs on GitHub Actions: - Python CI runs on every push and pull request to main. It covers Python 3.10–3.13 and runs ruff (lint and format), mypy in strict mode, ty as a second type checker, unit tests, and integration tests against Neo4j in Docker. Coverage is reported to Codecov. - TypeScript CI and end-to-end tests run on every push and pull request. - A conformance (TCK) suite runs nightly against the published npm package. - A hosted-service integration suite runs on every push to main. - Docs are built with Antora and checked for broken links, rendered layout, and executable snippets. API docs are generated with TypeDoc. - Releases are tag-driven. Python packages publish to PyPI through OIDC Trusted Publishing, with no long-lived tokens. TypeScript packages publish to npm. - Dependabot manages dependency updates. Cadence: 15 Python releases between January and September 2026, roughly every 2–4 weeks through May. Releases are recorded in a Keep-a-Changelog CHANGELOG.md. ### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications The memory data model, the MCP tool profile, and the conformance suite act as the project's specification today. Changes go through public pull requests on GitHub and are recorded in CHANGELOG.md. If accepted, we will formalize this as a versioned specification. Changes would follow a public RFC process (a proposals/ directory, with a minimum comment period and maintainer approval), and every specification change would need matching conformance tests ### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker https://github.com/neo4j-labs/agent-memory/issues ### External Project Dependencies

Core runtime:

Current decision process: maintainers decide by lazy consensus on pull requests and issues. The project lead makes the call on roadmap and release scope. Under AAIF: the project will move to an MVG-style maintainer council. Decisions will be made by lazy consensus and escalated to a majority vote of maintainers if needed, with technical direction discussed in public issues. ### Roadmap - A versioned memory specification, with the TCK expanded to cover it. - A pluggable openCypher storage backend interface, including an embedded backend. - Ontology-aware extraction: user-defined schemas and validation modes. - Import and export to open knowledge interchange formats (for example OKF). - Distilling reusable, provenance-grounded skills from reasoning memory. - Published results on public memory benchmarks (LongMemEval, STATE-Bench). - Deeper integrations with goose, A2A, and agentgateway. ### Security The project does not have an OpenSSF Best Practices badge yet; we plan to apply before onboarding. Current practices: - Dependabot updates for dependencies. - OIDC Trusted Publishing to PyPI, with no long-lived publish tokens. - Strict static typing (mypy strict plus ty). - Pinned dependency ranges with documented compatibility bounds. - Per-user namespace isolation in the SDK. - Parameterized Cypher throughout. ### Website URL https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/ ### Documented Governance Practices (if any) CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/MAINTAINING.md in the repository. GOVERNANCE.md and MAINTAINERS.md will be added as part of onboarding. ### Links to Social Media Accounts _No response_ ### Trademark and accounts - [x] If the project is accepted, I agree to donate all project trademarks and accounts to the AAIF. ### Details of Existing Financial Sponsorship Neo4j, Inc. funds development through employed maintainers and covers CI and documentation hosting. There is no external financial sponsorship. ### Infrastructure Needs or Requests - A new GitHub organization or repository location under AAIF. - CI capacity for Docker-based database integration tests, which would benefit from larger runners. - Documentation hosting and a project domain. - Transfer or renaming of the PyPI and npm package namespaces. ### Additional Information We are applying at the Sandbox level. Persistent memory is a critical gap in the AAIF stack, and we want to build multi-organization maintainership under neutral governance. The open-source SDKs, MCP server, data model, and conformance suite are fully usable on their own: users can self-host against their own database. Neo4j's commercial hosted service is a separate offering and is not part of this proposal. ### Application contact name(s) and email(s) William Lyon william.lyon@neo4j.com, Michael Hunger michael.hunger@neo4j.com, Stephen Chin [stephen.chin@neo4j.com](mailto:stephen.chin@neo4j.com) ### Contributing or sponsoring entity signatory information If an organization: | Name | Address | Type (e.g., Delaware corporation) | Signatory name and title | Email address | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------| | Neo4j, Inc. | 400 Concar Dr. San Mateo, CA 94402 | Delaware corp | Michael Hunger VP Product Innovation | michael.hunger@neo4j.com |
